title: Bottom-up Heap Sort
definition: Bottom-up Heap Sort is a variation of heap sort that builds the heap by processing nodes from the bottom up rather than the traditional top-down approach. This method can be more efficient than the standard build-heap approach because it starts heapification from the leaves and moves upward, taking advantage of the fact that subtrees near the leaves are already heaps.
conceptExplanation: In bottom-up heap sort, the heap is built starting from the lowest level and moving upward. Unlike the traditional approach that starts from the last non-leaf node and moves up, the bottom-up approach processes nodes in reverse level order. This can reduce the number of heapify operations needed. After building the heap, the extraction phase is the same as standard heap sort: repeatedly swap the root with the last element, reduce heap size, and heapify the root.
keyPoints: - Bottom-up heap construction - More efficient build-heap - O(n) build-heap - Same extraction phase as standard heap sort - In-place sort
importantTerminology: Bottom-up Heap Sort, Bottom-up heapify, Build-heap, Extraction
workingPrinciple:
The algorithm starts heapification from the bottom level of the tree and moves upward. Traditional build-heap starts from floor(n/2)-1 and goes up. Bottom-up processes nodes in reverse level order (from last level to first). This is more efficient because when heapifying a node, its children (which are at lower levels) may already satisfy the heap property from previous operations. After heap construction, the extraction phase is identical to standard heap sort: swap root with last element, reduce heap size, heapify root.

Mathematically, the bottom-up build-heap performs fewer comparisons than the traditional top-down approach, though both are O(n). The constant factor is better for bottom-up.
realLifeExample: Efficient heap construction when memory hierarchy favors bottom-up processing, embedded systems
dsaExample: Sorting array [12, 11, 13, 5, 6, 7] using bottom-up heap sort: build heap bottom-up → [13, 11, 12, 5, 6, 7], extract 13 → swap with 7 → [7, 11, 12, 5, 6, 13] (13 sorted), heapify → [11, 7, 12, 5, 6], ... → final sorted
diagram: Bottom-up heap sort: array of 6 elements. Traditional starts from index 2 (floor(6/2)-1). Bottom-up starts from leaves (indices 5, 4, then 2, 1). The heap shape is the same, but the order of heapify operations differs.
algorithm:
Bottom-up Heap Sort Algorithm:
1. BOTTOM-UP-BUILD-MAX-HEAP(arr)
2. FOR i = n DOWNTO 2
3.   SWAP arr[1] WITH arr[i]
4.   HEAP-SIZE = HEAP-SIZE - 1
5.   MAX-HEAPIFY(arr, 1)
6. END FOR

BOTTOM-UP-BUILD-MAX-HEAP(arr):
1. SET heap-size = n
2. FOR i = n DOWNTO floor(n/2) + 1
3.   (No action needed - leaves are already heaps)
4. END FOR
5. FOR i = floor(n/2) DOWNTO 1
6.   MAX-HEAPIFY(arr, i)
7. END FOR

This processes from the bottom level upward, ensuring children are heaps before parent.
pseudocode:
BEGIN
  FUNCTION bottomUpBuildMaxHeap(arr)
    SET n = length(arr)
    SET heap-size = n
    // Process from bottom level upward
    // First, handle nodes at the lowest level
    FOR i = n DOWNTO floor(n/2) + 1
      // Leaves are already valid heaps (single nodes)
    END FOR
    // Then heapify from last non-leaf node upward
    FOR i = floor(n/2) DOWNTO 1
      maxHeapify(arr, i)
    END FOR
  END FUNCTION

  FUNCTION heapSort(arr)
    bottomUpBuildMaxHeap(arr)
    FOR i = length(arr) DOWNTO 2
      SWAP arr[1] WITH arr[i]
      SET heap-size = heap-size - 1
      maxHeapify(arr, 1)
    END FOR
    RETURN arr
  END FUNCTION
END
complexity:
Time: O(n log n) overall
- Build heap: O(n) with optimal gap sequence
- Extraction phase: O(n log n) - n-1 heapify calls each O(log n)
- Total: O(n log n)
Space: O(1 The time complexity of heap sort with bottom-up build is O(n log n 1) - in-place

Note: Both shell's original sequence and knuth sequence give same asymptotic complexity, but constant factors differ
applications: When O(1) space is needed with guaranteed O(n log n) performance, educational purposes to show gap sequence variations
advantages: O(n) build phase with proper gap sequence, in-place, no recursion overhead
limitations: Complexity analysis depends on gap sequence choice, less commonly implemented, harder to analyze than standard heap sort
commonMistakes: Incorrect gap sequence, wrong index calculations for left/right children, confusing with shell sort (different algorithm)

fiveMarkQuestions.question: Explain heap sort algorithm and bottom-up variant.
fiveMarkQuestions.answer:
Heap Sort: Uses binary heap data structure. Two phases:

1. Build-Max-Heap: Start from floor(n/2)-1, heapify each node up to root. Ensures max element at root.

Extract: Swap root with last element, reduce heap size, heapify root. Repeat n-1 times.

Complexity: Always O(n log n), O(1) space.

Bottom-up Heap Sort: Variation where build-heap starts from leaves and moves upward. Gap sequence affects performance

tenMarkQuestions.question: Explain heap sort with bottom-up and top-down approaches.
tenMarkQuestions.answer:
Heap Sort: Uses binary heap structure. Two-phase algorithm.

Build-Max-Heap: Start from floor(n/2)-1 (0-based), call heapify moving upward to root. Ensures max element at root. Can be done in O(n).

Extraction Phase: Swap arr[0] with arr[i] (i from n-1 to 2), reduce heap size, heapify root. After n-1 extractions, array sorted.

Complexity: Always O(n log n), Space O(1).

Bottom-up Heap Sort: Gap sequence starts large (n/2) and reduces to 1. Each gap performs gapped insertion sort. Final gap=1 is standard insertion sort. Shell's original sequence: n/2, n/4, ..., 1. Complexity depends on gap choice.

Top-down Heap Sort: Traditional approach - build heap from last non-leaf node upward. More straightforward, widely used.

Stability: Not stable in both cases.

Applications: When O(n log n) guaranteed with O(1) space needed. Embedded systems, priority queues.
